# The report

Read at step 6: the report holds every item below, in this order.

- every node written, by identifier — on a populated root, created, changed and removed listed
  apart;
- the impact set that was read — in the specification and, on evolution, in the plan — as step 1's
  `--impact` output verbatim, beside the terms grepped to nominate its candidates. The output says
  the closure ran; the terms are what a reviewer argues with;
- every fact the decided-fact route wrote into the specification, in the order they surfaced: each
  `decided` outcome by its log entry — the node and field it filled, what was unstated, the value
  and the why, as the writer's first line names it — and each `stated` outcome with where the
  material already held it, and its log entry where that was under `intake/`. Name with each the
  skeleton and re-bind that surfaced it, so a chain of facts under one skeleton reads as a chain,
  and any criterion reworded on the way with the wording it lost. Every `noticed` watch item
  follows;
- every blocking note, by task identifier, with what it concedes — the tasks not yet written, or
  written with a standing conflict;
- every note a binder returned, by task identifier, as written into each task's `## Notes` — an
  underdetermined one with the implementation it names, a remainder one with where it belongs;
- every node carrying `rationale`, by identifier;
- where a standard was named: where it resolved from — the invocation, or the project file by path
  — what it presupposes, and where each artifact stands: held by the tree, or produced by a task
  this plan holds, by identifier and path. Where none resolved, which absence it was — a declared
  none, or nothing anywhere. Where one resolved, also the constraints this plan's tasks implement
  that no step decides: those are held by reading alone;
- which steps, if any, ran inline instead of in a subagent, each with the spawn failure that
  allowed it, verbatim;
- the validator's final output, verbatim;
- the handoff: the `/implement-task` invocation ready to paste, with the project root, the target
  and the initiative's slug filled in, and the project's standard where the project file does not
  already answer it. **The task** is the one slot left open: one invocation carries one task, and
  choosing it is choosing what gets built. In its place, offer where the deliverable set is read,
  as a command rather than a list: `deliver.py --outstanding <delivery-root> <work-root>
  <target-source-root> <specification-root>`, every root resolved, which names per task what has
  no record and what it waits on, then the set itself. A set restated here would be true only when
  printed. Where that set holds more than one task, `bin/deliver.py --help` describes delivering
  them in parallel, one worktree per task, integrated by merge — the person's choice, like
  everything in the handoff. The handoff offers the next step and never takes it: filling the open
  slot and invoking are the person's, per invocation or once for a whole route through
  `/deliver-scope`, whose own file bounds what it may fill.
